findings.description: The rewrite of §8 replaced "A `spec` finding's `suggestion` is always `null`" with "A `suggestion` that `review-spec` wrote is always `null`". That rule now depends on who wrote the suggestion. But the orchestrator writes suggestions too: the checklist (L183) says "write `body` and `suggestion` for every important", and §8 is addressed to the orchestrator. With `review-spec` now always returning a null suggestion (review-spec.md L14), the remaining way issue text reaches a committable block is the orchestrator writing one from `review-spec`'s description, which quotes the issue. That covers a `spec`-area finding and one moved into `correctness`/`security` by §6 or a merge. The old wording blocked this for `spec`-area findings. The new wording blocks it for none. The poster (tools/review/src/post-review.script.ts L74-78) renders any non-null suggestion as a committable ```suggestion``` block when the anchor isn't relocated. The fix is to key on the finding's origin instead of on who wrote the suggestion.
findings.body:
This change ties the null-suggestion rule to who wrote the suggestion, and removes the old area-based rule ("A `spec` finding's `suggestion` is always `null`").

The orchestrator writes `suggestion` too. Two places say so:
- The checklist, [SKILL.md#L183](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/cc5306c60d53a6d14d8a2ca6237f1a679c2741d9/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L183-L183): "write `body` and `suggestion` for every important".
- The §8 bullets, which address the orchestrator directly.

`review-spec` now always returns `null` ([review-spec.md#L14](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/cc5306c60d53a6d14d8a2ca6237f1a679c2741d9/.claude/agents/review-spec.md#L14-L14)). One path is left: the orchestrator writes a suggestion from `review-spec`'s description, which quotes issue text that anyone may have written. That path works for a `spec` finding, and for one §6 or a merge moved to `correctness`/`security`.

Nothing downstream catches it:
- `review-validator.md` never looks at `suggestion`.
- The schema doesn't tie `suggestion` to `area`.
- `tools/review/src/post-review.script.ts` L74-78 renders any non-null suggestion as a committable ```` ```suggestion ```` block unless it had to move the anchor.

The old wording blocked this for `spec` findings; the new wording blocks it for none.

[SKILL.md#L154](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/cc5306c60d53a6d14d8a2ca6237f1a679c2741d9/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L154-L154)

Fix: base the rule on where the finding came from (any finding `review-spec` raised), not on who writes the suggestion.
findings.suggestion: - **`suggestion` is committable code, so it must be exactly right.** Only for a small self-contained fix that resolves the finding entirely. The poster renders it as an inert fence rather than a committable block whenever it had to relocate the anchor, since applying it there would rewrite a line the finding never mentioned. A finding `review-spec` raised has a `null` `suggestion`, whoever would write it and whatever area the finding ends up in (§6), a merge included: its fix would rest on issue text, which the validator can only check against that same text (why `--fix` skips a `spec` finding).

findings.description: Local `--fix` still decides by area alone: "apply each confirmed finding except a `spec` one". A `review-spec` finding that §6 moves to `correctness`/`security`, or merges into another reviewer's finding, is still applied automatically. The orchestrator writes that edit from a description quoting issue text, which is the same provenance gap this delta closed for suggestions. The L154 text this delta added justifies itself with "(why `--fix` skips a `spec` finding)", so the two rules now use different keys. The impact is limited to a local run with a user present who sees the edit and the post-verify. The fix is to skip any finding `review-spec` raised, not only `spec`-area ones.
